alternatives_considered.approach: One shared validation helper for create and update
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Create's active-only member set would refuse legitimate edits touching departed members (AC-3/AC-6); the update path needs its own active-UNION-expense-referenced member set.

alternatives_considered.approach: Skip the write and the feed entry when an untouched save moves nothing
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Conditional writes complicate the exactly-one-entry invariant (TR-17) and AC-6's rewrite expectation; always writing one entry with empty detail keeps the rule total and testable.

work_order.approach: Keep the proposal's shape (reuse the create path's write mechanics for edit/delete, shared ExpenseForm, edit page plus dialog delete) but rebuild it on the critique's corrected premises: the update path validates against active members UNION this expense's referenced members, reopen order is canonical member order extended to departed members, delete removes all three child row sets in-transaction, delete navigates via redirect after the transaction in an awaited continuation, the parent-row write is explicit and first (row lock serializing concurrent saves), untouched saves always write one empty-detail entry, the delete confirmation carries the id only, and the edit segment gets its own loading.tsx. Add the integration and component tests the proposal omitted.
assumptions: Archived groups are read-only for expense edit/delete (the action refuses); a person can overturn this.
Delete confirmation carries the expense id only and renders a fixed or server-resolved sentence, never URL-echoed text.
work_order.confidence_rationale: Root cause is verified in code for every blocking finding (active-only validation set, unmount-loses-effect navigation, child rows surviving soft delete, no ordinal column, $onUpdate vs byte-identical, missing test files), and the fixes are narrow and follow existing repo patterns (awaited continuation, in-statement guards, canonical order). What keeps this out of the 90s: concurrent-save serialization is reasoned from the row lock rather than load-proven, and the archived-group read-only call is an assumption a person has not confirmed.
work_order.debate_summary: The critique was right on all ten findings and I accepted every one, upgrading none and dismissing none: the active-member validation set (blocking), the unmount-loses-navigation delete redirect (blocking), child rows surviving soft delete (blocking), the missing reopen order vs remainder-to-first rule (major), zero test files for test-verified criteria (major), the delete-then-insert race (major), the byte-identical-vs-$onUpdate plus empty-detail contradiction (major), the forgeable confirmation parameter (minor), the missing edit loading.tsx (minor), and the unnamed parent-row write (minor). No finding contradicts a decision in plan/brief.md — the brief's stored-split-rule, wholesale in-transaction replace, and never-re-evaluate-history decisions are exactly what the accepted fixes enforce. I folded in the load-bearing missed edge cases (deleted-expense edit guard, idempotent double delete, departed-payer name coalesce, plain-text amount round-trip incl. JPY and percent/share units, empty-participants refusal, archived-group refusal, caller-leaves-before-save) and the regression risks (expense-list DOM reshape, expense-form mock missing updateExpense, create refusal sentences, dynamic route, exhaustive kind map).

qa_script: Seed, create an expense, open its edit page and confirm every field matches what was typed.
Edit amount, payers, participants and split type in one save; confirm balances move and the feed names each change.
Delete an expense via the naming dialog; confirm the list shows an in-place confirmation.
residual_risks: Concurrent overlapping saves serialize on the parent-row UPDATE by reasoning, not by load test — QA cannot easily cover this; watch for unique-violation 500s on double submit.
Archived-group read-only refusal is assumed, not person-confirmed; if the product wants archived edits, the guard must come out.
QA should prioritize: JPY/whole-unit and grouped-amount round-trips, emoji descriptions through reopen and diff, back-button onto a deleted expense's edit page, and double delete from two tabs.
risks: Extracting create validation into shared helpers risks changing create's exact refusal sentences; the integration suite asserting them must pass unchanged.
Wrapping expense-list rows in links reshapes the row subtree the existing DOM assertions pin; those assertions are revisited in the same change.
